units.spine: Nothing in Warmholz is arranged for buying and selling in quantity.
In Warmholz, nothing that could be somebody's job on the side has been made official.
The stock and the people of Warmholz have been pulled inward, and the ground given up stands abandoned.
None of this is urgent, and the difficulties are chronic rather than acute.
This is as far as Warmholz bends. Past this point the conditions belong to a different town, and that point is close.
It is getting worse, steadily rather than suddenly. The conditions here cost a little more each season than the one before.
Warmholz's year closes near enough to level that the closing is watched.
What gets counted about Warmholz is a fraction of what happens, and nobody chooses which fraction that is.
The terms Warmholz has to work with are what is under judgment, not the town itself.
Less stands between Warmholz and trouble than a town this size ought to have.
What protects Warmholz is that nobody has wanted it, and everyone here understands the arrangement.
Nobody in Warmholz has an answer for what lives beyond its fields, and it is nobody's job to find one.
There is more going on in Warmholz than anyone here troubles to follow, and none of it is hidden particularly well.
Warmholz's economy has no slack in it, and a careful eye notices the absence first.
Warmholz keeps no practitioner, no arrangement, and no expectation of either.
Nobody in Warmholz thinks about food.
Somebody, once, found this a reasonable distance from the last place, and that is why Warmholz stands here.
A handful of roofs with a reason is what Warmholz is, and the reason is usually the ground.
The people of Warmholz are connected to each other the way people anywhere settled are. Nothing about their ties beyond the hamlet stands out.
A careful eye on Warmholz turns up one loose end, and it is the kind a single institution would tie off.
